title: ARV spelled out as 'alien reproduction vehicle' in the briefing, seen as counterintelligence marker

tellings.quote: you know, to the best of my recollection, it was expanded as alien reproduction vehicle.

plain: A former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown says the secret Pentagon briefing on the program Immaculate Constellation spelled out the term ARV as "alien reproduction vehicle", meaning a craft copied from a nonhuman one, and he takes the spelling as a marker used to trace leaks. He tells Michels this in 2026, "to the best of my recollection", and he also mentions Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official. The unsigned public report on the program, which Brown later said he wrote, writes only "ARV/RV (Reproduction Vehicles)": it explains the "reproduction vehicle" part and leaves the A unexplained, so "alien" rests on his memory of a briefing that has not been made public.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report writes "ARV/RV (Reproduction Vehicles)", a gloss that spells out the RV and leaves the A unglossed. Matthew Brown's "alien reproduction vehicle" is his recollection of the classified briefing, which is not public, so the expansion rests on his memory of it.
